mappings.note: The liquid fuel used most in homes is science as it shows up in daily life. Not LO-17, because the item does not sort fuels into exhaustible and inexhaustible classes.
The elements making up petroleum is material composition, which LO-16 covers through properties and structure. Not LO-20, because no process of formation is explained.
The chief gas in LPG is the composition of a material. Not LO-27, because the item asks what it is rather than where it is used.
What CNG stands for identifies a material by its nature. Not LO-28, which is used here for choosing the cleaner fuel.
Where piped natural gas is supplied in India is an everyday application of the fuel. Not LO-17, since no resource classification is required.
Petroleum as black gold identifies a material from a familiar name. Not LO-26, because no discovery story is involved.
What the hydrogen from natural gas is used for is an industrial application in daily life. Not LO-21, because no reaction equation is written.
Petrochemicals traced to petroleum is the origin and composition of materials. Not LO-27, since no use is named.
Whether fossil fuels can be made in a laboratory turns on understanding how slowly they form, a process to explain. Not LO-17, because no resource class is assigned.
India's natural gas reserves is a fact about how much of a finite resource remains, the basis for judicious use. Not LO-17, because the item gives a quantity rather than a class.
Testing statements about fossil fuels rests on the characteristics that define that resource class. Not LO-20, because no process is explained.
Why natural gas counts as a clean fuel relates a property to its cause. Not LO-28, because the item explains rather than recommends.
How CNG is obtained, by compressing natural gas, is a process to explain. Not LO-16, because the item describes a treatment rather than a composition.
The methane percentage of natural gas is material composition. Grouped with the other composition items on LO-16.
Choosing the non-polluting fuel for vehicles is an environmental judgement about resource use. Not LO-27, which covers where a fuel is used rather than which is kinder to the air.
Picking the fossil fuel from a list is classification of natural resources. Not LO-16, because a class is assigned rather than properties compared.
The natural solid fuel sorts fuels by origin and state. Not LO-16, because the item asks for a class member rather than a property.
The non-polluting renewable source is the inexhaustible side of the resource classification LO-17 names verbatim. Not LO-28, because nothing is being conserved here, only classified.
Excluding the non-renewable source is the exhaustible/inexhaustible classification. Mirror of the previous item and coded the same way.
Petroleum meaning rock oil explains what the material is from its name. Not LO-26, because no discovery is recounted.
Natural gas being mostly methane is material composition. Grouped with the other composition items.
Which fuel supplies most of the world's energy is a fact about the standing of a resource class. Not LO-28, because no conservation measure is proposed.
The fuel that burns without polluting is an environmental choice between resources. Grouped with the clean-fuel-for-vehicles item rather than with the classification items.
Picking the exhaustible natural resource is LO-17's own example, word for word. Not LO-28, because no protective action follows.
Excluding the substance that is not a fuel sorts materials by a characteristic. Not LO-16, because membership rather than a property is tested.
The gas produced when coal burns in air is the product of a combustion reaction, the substance of LO-21's word equations. Not LO-20, which is used for the slow formation and distillation processes.
Carbonisation as the slow conversion of vegetation into coal is a process to be explained. Not LO-17, because no resource class is assigned.
Heating coal without air to give coke is the destructive distillation process. Not LO-21, because it is not a reaction with air, water or acid.
The purest form of carbon compares materials on a property. Not LO-17, because no class of resource is assigned.
Naming carbonisation as the slow conversion of dead vegetation is a process explanation. Duplicate in substance of the earlier carbonisation item.
The gas from burning coal in plentiful air is a combustion product. Grouped with the other reaction-product item rather than the process items.
What coke is used to manufacture is an industrial application of a material. Not LO-16, since the item asks the use, not the property.
Identifying coke from tough, porous and nearly pure carbon is identification by properties. Not LO-27, because no use is named.
Which substance is used in metal extraction is an application of a fuel product. Grouped with the other use items on LO-27.
Coal tar in perfume manufacture is an everyday application of a by-product. Not LO-16, because the item asks where it goes, not what it is.
Picking the exhaustible resource is the resource classification named in LO-17. Not LO-28, because nothing is conserved.
Picking the inexhaustible resource is the mirror of the same classification. Coded with its counterpart for the same reason.
The body advising drivers how to save fuel is an organised effort at judicious resource use. Not LO-27, because the item is about conserving rather than using.
Bitumen for road metalling is an application of a petroleum product. Grouped with the other use items.
The petroleum fraction used as a dry-cleaning solvent is an everyday application. Not LO-16, because the use rather than the property is asked for.
